language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<meta>Single woodblock-printed folio in red ink inside a ruled double frame. The Chinese margin label sits on the right edge as the image is shown. A short Mongolian marginal label, probably the title or folio number, sits in the narrow side panel at the opposite end. The leaf is shown rotated 90°.</meta>

Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the Vinaya Masters, Volume Six, Part One, Folio Three <note>original: "律師戒行經第六卷上三". This Chinese margin label gives the title, volume and leaf number. Bilingual labels like this helped binders and readers keep the loose leaves of Mongolian Buddhist woodblock prints in order. The word 上 "upper" probably marks the first part of the volume.</note>

<summary>Folio 3 of the first part of Volume Six of a Mongolian Vinaya text on monastic discipline, printed from woodblocks in red ink. Only the Chinese margin label, which gives the title and folio number, could be read. The Mongolian body text was not transcribed.</summary>
